Laura / Finance team —

We have Eben (strong infra background) preferring to stay in Berlin. Recruiter requests guidance on whether we can offer a location premium to match a competitor's ~12% uplift vs our US-converted band.

Quick context: role level L4 (IC), original US comp band for L4 converted to EUR puts him ~8% below competitor. Recruiter suggests either:
- Option A: increase base by one sub-band (~8–12%) to match market (ongoing); or
- Option B: keep band but offer a one-time "localization sign-on" to bridge the gap (tax/benefits implications).

Questions:
1) Can we apply a recurring location uplift for EU hires, or do we prefer one-time bridges?
2) What approvals do we need (headcount, comp manager signoff, legal for EUR payroll)?
3) If we do a one-time bridge, cap amounts?

Please advise — hiring manager (not on this thread yet) is ready to move quickly.

Thanks,
Rishi

Thanks for flagging. Short answers:
- I'm ok with a one-time localization sign-on to secure strong hires in strategic locations, provided it doesn't push total comp above midpoint of comparable EU peers.
- Prefer one-time for hiring velocity / tax simplicity. Only make recurring adjustments for roles where we plan to standardize local bands (we are not there yet in EU).
- Approval: hiring manager + People Ops + Finance (Vivek) needs to sign off; amounts < $15k one-time can be approved by me + Rishi; anything above goes to Neha for final approval.

For Eben specifically: if the gap is ~12% and would require > $15k one-time to bridge, escalate to Neha. Otherwise, proceed with one-time sign-on half in cash, half as restricted stock units (to align retention).

Please add hiring manager and send proposed numbers.

Laura
VP, Engineering (Hiring Lead)
Redwood Inference

Folks — attaching the latest comp-band grid and a short rubric for geo adjustments. Key points:
1) Base conversion: we keep US band anchors and map to local currency using a quarterly FX + local market multiplier. That typically puts EU markets at -5% to +5% of US-equivalent after conversion.
2) Localization premium: for high-demand EU cities (London, Berlin, Amsterdam) we allow a one-time localization sign-on capped at $18k USD total (global cap) or ongoing uplift of up to 10% only for roles where we explicitly maintain a local band (requires Product + People Ops approval).
3) Payroll/legal: offering EUR ongoing base requires local payroll setup or PEO; one-time payments can be run through payroll as sign-on with tax withholding, but equity SSR treatment varies — coordinate with Neha for EUR RSU issuance.

For Eben: based on the competing offer and CV, recommended path:
- Offer: mapped base to EU L4 band (EUR equivalent) + one-time localization bridge of $12k USD (payable 50% cash / 50% RSU vesting 1 year cliff) — falls under Laura + Rishi approval (sub-$15k rule).
- If hiring manager insists on full ongoing uplift, Neha must greenlight and we may need to adjust headcount budget.

I've attached the comp-band grid: 2027-04-comp-band-grid.xlsx and the short rubric. If you want, I can run budget impact numbers for the Berlin org line.

-Vivek
Director, People Finance
Redwood Inference
